splits.cell_id: global row index in data/processed/cite/cite_arrays.npz (bridge export id cite_site4_<index>)

test_primary.rule: site4 cells of donors not in training

test_secondary.rule: site4 cells of donor 15078 (in training at sites 1-3)

annotation_map_notes.gdT CD158b+: T by lineage (gamma-delta TCR, CD3 protein). They carry NK receptors (CD158b, CD56, CD94); the protein gate decides whether each one enters the key as T (CD3 high) or is unscored. Sensitivity key 'primary_no_gdT158' drops them.
annotation_map_notes.gdT TCRVD2+: T (Vdelta2 gamma-delta T; CD3 protein high).
annotation_map_notes.T prog cycling: T: annotated as a T-committed cycling population; 24 training cells, none in val or site4.
annotation_map_notes.CD4+ T CD314+ CD45RA+: T; 92 training cells, 1 val, none in site4.
annotation_map_notes.CD8+ T naive CD127+ CD26- CD101-: T; 42 training cells, none in val or site4.
annotation_map_notes.cDC1: myeloid (conventional DC, like cDC2); 18 training cells, none in val or site4.
annotation_map_notes.cDC2: myeloid (conventional DC; CD11c and CD33 protein high).
annotation_map_notes.pDC: OUT: plasmacytoid DCs are not monocytes or conventional DCs and carry none of the four lineage panels (CD123/CD303 high, CD11c low); a lineage call on them is wrong.
annotation_map_notes.ILC: OUT: innate lymphoid cells lack a TCR and are not conventional NK cells. Many are NK-like in protein (CD56/CD94 high); they then gate NK and are unscored, not keyed NK.
annotation_map_notes.ILC1: OUT: as ILC. In this dataset most annotated ILC1 are CD3-protein high (T-like); those gate T and are unscored.
annotation_map_notes.Plasma cell IGKC+: OUT: antibody-secreting cells are a terminal B-lineage state outside the mature-B panel question (CD19 partly, CD20 low, CD38 very high).
annotation_map_notes.Lymph prog: OUT: progenitor (B-committed in part; many are CD19 protein high and then unscored).
annotation_map_notes.HSC: OUT: stem cells; no lineage panel applies.

rules_in_order: T if CD3 high and no B marker high and CD14 not high
B if CD3 not high and a B marker high and CD14 not high
NK if CD3, B markers, CD14 and CD33 not high and at least nk_min_high of the NK markers high
myeloid if CD3 and B markers not high and any of CD14 / CD11c / CD33 high

selection.criterion: highest mean per-batch Cohen kappa (gate vs annotation, 5 classes) over the 8 training batches (site x donor); ties -> fewer markers; confirmed on val

sensitivity_keys.annotation_only: annotation class for every cell (OUT included)
sensitivity_keys.primary_per_batch: agreement of annotation with a gate whose thresholds are re-estimated within each site x donor batch by the same declared estimator (label-free; uses the batch's own measured protein, so it is a verifier variant, never evidence)

no_gdT158.rule: primary key with gdT CD158b+ cells set to unscored

teddy_head.head: phase-1 MLP + NB decoder mean (no flow matching), outputs/cite_phase1_official/best.pt
teddy_head.normaliser: 95th percentile of the head's prediction over the training cells (split=train), per protein
teddy_head.why_size_factor_cancels: prediction = softplus(.) * s for a constant s, and the training q95 scales by the same s, so the evidence is independent of s; no measured-protein array enters the evidence path

selection.score: worst-pair AUROC: for class k, the minimum over every other primary-key class c (OUT included, classes with >= 10 val cells) of the AUROC of the unclipped normalised head prediction for k versus c; ties by one-vs-rest AUROC, then name
selection.rule: each protein is assigned to the class where its worst-pair AUROC is highest; a class panel is its top 3 assigned proteins with worst-pair AUROC >= 0.8
selection.criteria_computed_and_not_used: one-vs-rest AUROC (saturates: many proteins within 0.002 of 1 on val) and Cohen's d (scale- and clip-dependent); both tables are in the dev log

stability_same_rule_on_training_cells.note: diagnostic only, on a seeded sample of 20,000 training primary-key cells (in-sample for the head)

canonical9_plus_nk.note: old canonical 9-marker panel (chosen on site4 Pearson in v1/v2) plus the val-selected NK panel minus any protein already in it

canonical9_variant_plus_nk.note: canonical panel with CD20 for CD72 and CD14 for CD36, plus the val-selected NK panel

Q1.name: soft 4-class lineage question
Q1.text: From the TEDDY + head evidence, is this cell B, T, NK or myeloid? Call the class with the highest panel score if that score reaches the bar; otherwise no call.
Q1.score: equal-weight mean of the evidence over the class panel

Q2.name: strict 4-class lineage question
Q2.text: As Q1 with a higher bar (nested: every Q2 call is a Q1 call with the same class).

Q3.name: CD14-anchored question (B / T / NK / classical monocyte)
Q3.text: Is this cell a B cell (CD19), T cell (CD3), NK cell (CD56) or a classical CD14+ monocyte (CD14)? Score each class by its one canonical anchor protein; call the highest if it reaches the bar; otherwise no call. Non-classical monocytes and dendritic cells are not an answer (no call).
Q3.score: evidence of the class anchor protein

key.rule: primary-key myeloid: annotated classical monocyte AND measured CD14 high -> myeloid; annotated other myeloid AND measured CD14 not high -> OUT (no call correct); else unscored

anm.engine: ANM finite_field_runner (ANM_ROOT, public v2 fix branch), kind finite_graph_scalar
anm.event_timing: simultaneous: every evidence event of a cell at t = 0
anm.event_value: evidence v_p in [0, 1] (no weight: equal weights within a class)
anm.readout_thresholds_note: informational (rounded); v3_key.anm_readout_threshold recomputes field_gain(n) * n * bar exactly from the field parameters and the registered bar
anm.equivalence: with equal panel sizes and simultaneous events the ANM action score is field_gain(n) * n * S for every class, so ANM's calls equal the re-coded fixed rule's on every cell (checked cell by cell in E1; any mismatch is a failure)
anm.closure_readout_note: readout_coordinates over each action's event sites (ANM readout defaults); used only for C2 (nested readouts); its re-coded rule is reported beside it

primary.model: multinomial logistic regression (sklearn LogisticRegression, lbfgs, max_iter 3000)
primary.features: the primary-panel evidence (12 values, same as the rule and ANM)
primary.labels: primary key on training cells (5 classes incl. OUT; unscored excluded)
primary.C_selection: lowest val log-loss on val primary-key cells
primary.decision: call the lineage with the highest probability if that probability reaches the bar; otherwise no call (an OUT-probable cell has low lineage probabilities)
primary.bar_rule: val quantile matching the question's declared val no-call rate

secondary.model: sklearn MLPClassifier(hidden_layer_sizes=(64,), alpha=1e-4, early_stopping=True, validation_fraction=0.1, max_iter=500, random_state=seed)

q3.features: primary-panel evidence plus the Q3 anchors not already in it

e3.pairs_rule: k = 10 cosine neighbours on the raw L2-normalised final z within the evaluated split; each neighbour edge kept once; NK-T pair = one primary-key NK and one primary-key T cell
e3.flag_rule: sufficiency-flagged pair: cosine >= flag_cosine (TEDDY puts the two cells closer than the median val NK-T neighbour pair)

e2_subset.rule: seeded (seed 7) uniform sample without labels: 500 cells per primary donor, 250 from donor 15078

arm_names.classifier: TEDDY + trained classifier (same evidence, labels from training sites only)
arm_names.margin: TEDDY margin (top-1 minus top-2 rule score; a confidence score, not a separate decision)
arm_names.declared_rule: declared rule: used wherever ANM's field does not run (e.g. a trust-weighted average); never called ANM

common.evidence_rule: every compared method reads the same evidence values of the same cells; no method reads measured protein or annotation of an evaluated cell

metrics.coverage: fraction of all cells of the evaluated split that receive a call (label-free denominator; unscored cells included)
metrics.selective_accuracy: among called cells that are scored by the key: fraction whose call equals the key; a call on a key-OUT cell is wrong
metrics.decision_accuracy: among scored cells: correct call, or no call on a key-OUT cell
metrics.out_decline_rate: fraction of key-OUT cells with no call
metrics.per_class: recall per key class; call table per annotated cell type (all 40 site4 types); calls on unscored cells reported separately

matched_coverage.rule: at coverage c each method calls its ceil(c * N) most confident cells of the evaluated split (N = all cells of the split; ties broken by global cell index); this uses only each method's own scores, never labels
matched_coverage.aurc: area under selective accuracy vs coverage over the grid (trapezoid), divided by the coverage range 0.45
matched_coverage.operating_point: each method's deployed bar (from val) is also reported with its realised site4 coverage

confidence_scores.anm: top ANM action score (a fixed multiple of the rule's top score; identical ranking)

statistics.bootstrap: two-stage: resample donors with replacement, then cells (or pairs) with replacement within each drawn donor; B = 2000; seed = registration seeds.bootstrap; percentile 95% interval
statistics.per_donor: every endpoint is also reported per donor (19593, 13272; secondary 15078)
statistics.two_donor_caveat: the primary split has 2 donors, so the interval reflects the spread of the observed donors and cannot support population claims
statistics.win: point difference >= margin AND bootstrap 95% lower bound > 0 AND the difference has the same sign and is >= margin/2 in each primary donor
statistics.loss: mirror of win (difference <= -margin, upper bound < 0, both donors)
statistics.secondary_split: donor 15078 is reported with the same rules and never changes a primary verdict

common.reporting: report every pre-registered endpoint, including failures and inconclusive results; no site4 rerun with changed settings; anything decided after site4 is opened is labelled exploratory
common.addenda: a builder may fix a number not given here only by a procedure written here, only from train/val cells, and must write it to registration/addenda/<experiment>.json, record its sha256 in registration/addenda/HASHES.txt and commit it before any site4 evaluation; v3_leakage_check.py must pass for that builder
common.outputs: /Users/tianchichen/Documents/GitHub/teddy_mm/outputs/v3/<experiment>/ : <experiment>_results.json, REPORT.md, progress.log; every result JSON carries registration_sha256

E1.name: Mode B rerun on the v3 key: Experiments 1, 3, 4, 5 and C2 (nested readouts)
E1.key: primary (Q1, Q2); q3 (Q3); sensitivity: annotation_only, primary_per_batch, primary_no_gdT158
E1.panels: primary; sensitivity rows: canonical9_plus_nk, canonical9_variant_plus_nk, val_k2, val_k5 (rule and classifier; ANM on the primary panel)

arms: classifier trained on Q1 labels answering Q3 without relabelling
classifier trained on Q3 labels (all training-site labels)

endpoints.E1.1a: cells where ANM's call differs from the re-coded rule's (Q1, Q2, Q3); pre-registered value 0
endpoints.E1.1b: fraction of cells whose call changes Q1 -> Q2 and Q1 -> Q3 (descriptive), per annotated type
endpoints.E1.1c: Q3 selective accuracy on the q3 key at the rule's realised Q3 coverage: rule vs Q1 classifier without relabelling
endpoints.E1.1d: same, rule vs Q3 classifier (label-rich ceiling)

exp1_change_the_question.failure: any E1.1a mismatch means the bridge differs from its declared rule: stop and fix before any interpretation; 'zero labels to change the question' holds for any written rule and is reported as such, not as an ANM property

exp3_why_this_call.anm: leave-one-out over the called class's events (events at t = 0); top-1 marker = the event whose removal lowers the called action's score most; flip = the removal changes the call
exp3_why_this_call.rule: closed form: top-1 marker = the panel protein with the largest evidence in the called class (equal weights); flip when S_called - v_p / 3 falls below the bar or below another class score

endpoints.E1.3a: agreement of ANM's top-1 marker with the closed form (pre-registered expectation 1.000; below 0.99 is reported as a discrepancy)
endpoints.E1.3b: per-donor share of each top-1 marker (descriptive); null = within-class permutation of marker identities per cell, 1000 permutations (no slot-preserving null)
endpoints.E1.3c: error rate of flip-sensitive calls vs the same number of lowest-margin calls

exp3_why_this_call.win: flip-sensitive calls have a higher error rate than the matched lowest-margin calls by >= 0.02 (win rules): attribution flags errors beyond the margin
exp3_why_this_call.failure: otherwise attribution adds no flagging value beyond TEDDY's margin

exp4_which_calls_to_trust.comparison: ANM soft score vs TEDDY margin (primary); vs classifier and entropy (secondary)
exp4_which_calls_to_trust.failure: if ANM is not a win against the margin, the gate claim stays withdrawn

exp5_label_cost.question: Q3 (also Q1 for reference)
exp5_label_cost.labels: uniform random draws from training-site cells scored by the q3 key; n in [0, 25, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, all]; n = 0 is the Q1 classifier without relabelling; draws use seeds.label_cost_draws
exp5_label_cost.classifier: registration classifier.q3 (features, C); with a single class in a draw the classifier predicts that class
exp5_label_cost.endpoint: E1.5: n* = smallest n whose median-over-draws selective accuracy at the rule's realised Q3 coverage is >= the rule's minus 0.005
comparators: anm (0 labels, identical to the rule)
exp5_label_cost.note: a measurement, not a win/loss test; zero labels holds for the fixed rule as well as for ANM

c2_nested_readouts.nested_pair: outer readout P_f = a call is made under the question's bar; inner readout Q_f = the call equals the key; Q2 calls are a subset of Q1 calls
arms: anm closure readout (readout_coordinates over each action's event sites, ANM defaults)
re-coded closure rule (must equal ANM closure on every cell)
c2_nested_readouts.endpoint: E1.C2: key-OUT decline rate in test_primary at matched overall coverage c in {rule's realised Q1 coverage, 0.8, 0.7}, with in-scope selective accuracy beside it
c2_nested_readouts.win: ANM closure declines >= 0.05 more key-OUT cells than the mean rule at the same coverage (win rules) while its in-scope selective accuracy is not lower by more than 0.005
c2_nested_readouts.failure: if not a win, ANM's nested readout does not decline out-of-scope cells better than the rule; the re-coded closure rule always equals ANM closure, so any win is a property of the readout form, which a written rule also implements

E1.falsification: ANM adds decision value in Mode B only through an ANM-specific readout; this is falsified for v3 if C2 and Exp. 4 are not wins

E2.name: Response decomposition (C3) and linearity (C5) under input perturbation
E2.cells: registration e2_subset (1,000 test_primary + 250 test_secondary cells; drawn without labels)
E2.pipeline: official TEDDY-G preprocessing exactly as data/processed/cite_official/z_rna_manifest.json (counts/total x 1e4, divide by TEDDY gene medians, top 2,048 tokens, fp16 autocast, gene-mean) -> frozen phase-1 head -> registered evidence -> Q1 rule and ANM

rna_thinning.method: binomial thinning of each UMI count

gene_scaling.method: multiply the gene's official value by (1 - epsilon) before ranking (epsilon = 1 masks the gene)
gene_scaling.cells: only cells in which the gene is among the cell's tokens

genes.ensembl: symbols are mapped with a GRCh38 reference recorded in the E2 addendum; the 13 NK/T genes reuse the IDs in scripts/mode_a_token_probes.py; genes absent from the 12,052-gene vocabulary are dropped and listed

perturbations.floor: re-embed every unperturbed cell once to measure the numerical floor (fp16)

E2.measurements: per cell and perturbation: dz = ||z' - z|| (L2-normalised z); dv = ||v' - v|| over the 12 panel evidences; dS = change of the called class's score and of the margin; dANM = change of ANM's action score of the baseline call; dcall = call changed

linearity_C5.test: slope ratio rho = ||d(eps)|| / (2 ||d(eps/2)||) and cosine(d(eps), d(eps/2)) for dz, dv and dS; a cell is in the linear regime at a level if |rho - 1| <= 0.1, cosine >= 0.9 and ||d(eps/2)|| > 3 x floor
linearity_C5.endpoint: E2.lin: fraction of cells in the linear regime per level and stage (descriptive; thinning uses the seed-averaged response)

decomposition_C3.z_probe: multinomial logistic regression on L2-normalised z of training primary-key cells, C chosen on val by log-loss from [0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100] (addendum)
decomposition_C3.labels_per_lost_cell: for a cell correct and called at baseline but wrong or not called after the perturbation: 'representation' if the z-probe's class on z' is wrong; else 'head' if the rule's argmax on v' is wrong; else 'decision' (right class below the bar)
decomposition_C3.endpoint: E2.dec: shares of representation / head / decision among lost cells per perturbation family and level

E2.comparator: the plain perturbation -> accuracy curve (Q1 selective and decision accuracy vs epsilon)
E2.falsification: the decomposition adds information beyond the curve only if (i) two perturbations with accuracy losses within 0.02 of each other differ by >= 0.15 in a localisation share, or (ii) the small-eps response (dS at eps = 0.05 thinning, linearly extrapolated) predicts which cells change call at eps = 0.8 with AUROC >= 0.02 above baseline margin alone (bootstrap lower bound > 0); if neither holds, it adds nothing beyond the curve
E2.compute: about 0.118 s per cell embedding (official run, MPS fp16); 1,250 cells x (12 thinning + 1 floor + 3 per expressed gene) embeddings

E3.name: NK-T look-alike pairs under the v3 key (C4) and their repair on frozen TEDDY
E3.cells: test_primary; pairs by registration e3.pairs_rule; flagged by e3.flag_cosine (from val); variants all and no_gdT158

readouts.head: registered phase-1 head
readouts.R1_mlp_layer_means: MLP on the 12 gene-mean layer outputs (z_rna_layer_means.npy, concatenated), 2 hidden layers of 256, dropout 0.1, Adam 1e-3, up to 30 epochs, early stopping on val MSE; trained on training-site cells; targets = measured panel proteins + CD335 and CD3, each / training q95 of measured, clipped to [0, 1]
readouts.R2_attention_pooling: one learned query attending over layer-12 gene-token states, linear output to the same targets; trained on 4,000 training-site cells (seeds.e3_token_subset; one third key-NK, one third key-T, one third other) with 1,000 val cells for early stopping; Adam 1e-3, up to 50 epochs
readouts.null_seed_replicate: the phase-1 head architecture retrained with seed 1 (scripts/04_train.py settings) as the regression-to-the-mean and instability null

E3.gap_ratio: per readout and protein p in {CD56, CD94, CD335, CD3}: median |predicted evidence difference| / median |measured evidence difference| within pairs; GR = mean over the 4 proteins; each readout normalised by the training q95 of its own predictions

endpoints.E3.H3a: D_R = [GR_R(flagged) - GR_head(flagged)] - [GR_R(unflagged) - GR_head(unflagged)] for R in {R1, R2}, minus the same quantity for the null; pre-registered: >= 0.05 with win rules (pairs resampled within donors)
endpoints.E3.H3a_pooling: D_R2 - D_R1 >= 0.05: the loss is in mean pooling
endpoints.E3.H3b: NK-vs-T selective accuracy among key-NK and key-T cells of test_primary at matched coverage 0.9 and 0.8: Q1 rule on head evidence vs on R1 / R2 evidence (confidence = top rule score)

trust_comparators: kNN label disagreement: share of the cell's 10 nearest training cells in z whose training key label differs from the call
E3.falsification: if neither R1 nor R2 reaches D_R >= 0.05 over the null, 'the NK-T loss is in the readout or pooling and is repairable on frozen TEDDY' is rejected for this dataset

E4.name: Experiment 2 redesigned: two-channel fusion (C6)
E4.key: E4 key from the measured primary-panel proteins: Q1 scoring on measured panel evidence (measured / training q95 of measured, clipped); call the argmax if the top score >= tau_K, else OUT; tau_K chosen on val by maximum Cohen kappa against the annotation class over [0.05, 0.10, ..., 0.60] (addendum). Secondary: v3 primary key (partly circular for channel 2, disclosed)

channels.channel1: TEDDY + head prediction of the 12 panel proteins from RNA (registered evidence)
channels.channel2: ridge regression from the measured non-panel proteins (the 122 proteins outside the primary panel) to the measured panel evidence, alpha on val from [0.1, 1, 10, 100, 1000]; trained on training cells; it never receives a panel protein's measured value; normalised by the training q95 of its own predictions

noise_levels.L2: 50% of channel-2 input proteins set to 0 per cell (seeds.e4_noise)

E4.trust: per channel and level on val: mean over the 12 panel proteins of max(0, Pearson(channel evidence, measured evidence)); ANM source_scale = trust / max of the two channels' trust (addendum)

methods.F0: channel 1 alone, Q1 rule; F0b channel 2 alone
methods.F1: simple average of the two channels' class scores (declared rule)
methods.F2: trust-weighted average (declared rule; equals ANM without contradiction events and with the field's gain)
methods.F3: stacker: logistic regression on the 8 channel class scores, trained on val per noise level
methods.F4: learned fusion: logistic regression on the 24 evidence values, trained on training cells at L0
methods.F5: TEDDY + ANM fusion: support events per channel (source_scale = trust), contradiction events (for each channel, its top class contradicts every other class with value = that channel's top score x 0.5), all events at t = 0, action readout; bar from val at no-call 0.15 (addendum)

controls: F5 with channel 2 at t = 2 (declared order) vs t = 0 (time-blind)
re-coded closed form of F5 (must equal F5 on every cell)
E4.endpoint: E4: selective accuracy at matched coverage 0.8 (and 0.9) averaged over L0-L3, E4 key, test_primary: F5 vs the best of F1-F4 (primary) and F5 vs F2 (field effect)

outcomes.field_adds_value: F5 wins against the best of F1-F4
outcomes.field_adds_nothing: F5 - F2 equivalent within 0.01 (an acceptable, reportable outcome)

E4.failure: if both channels' val trust differ by less than 0.01 at every level, the trust mechanism is untestable here; report so

E5.name: Mode A layer dynamics (C7): Jacobian-vector products through TEDDY's layers
E5.cells: unique test_primary cells in E3's NK-T pairs, at most 200 per primary donor (seeds.e5_cells)
E5.direction: NK-T direction per layer d_l = mean over training key-NK cells minus mean over training key-T cells of the gene-mean layer output (layers 1-12 from z_rna_layer_means.npy; input layer recomputed), unit-normalised
E5.perturbation: for each E2 gene present in the cell, delta h_0 at the gene's position = the gene's token embedding, unit-normalised; controls: random unit vectors at the same position and random other genes of the cell (seeds.e5_random_directions)
E5.jvp: delta h_l = J_l delta h_(l-1) via torch.func.jvp through each actual encoder layer (fp32, CPU, eval mode, bool key-padding mask, standard Python path), delta z_l = masked gene-mean of delta h_l; r_l = <delta z_l, d_l>; layer gain g_l = |r_l| / |r_(l-1)|
E5.check: central finite differences at eps in {1e-2, 1e-3}: relative error <= 0.05 and cosine >= 0.99 at eps = 1e-3 for >= 95% of (cell, gene) cases; otherwise E5 stops with 'JVP not validated'
E5.endpoint: E5: layer l* with the most negative median log g_l for the NK-T component; compared with the layer at which the linear NK-T protein-probe gap ratio drops most in outputs/mode_a_official/mode_a_results.json
E5.falsification: if the JVP fails the finite-difference check, a linear-response description of TEDDY's layers is not valid at this scale; if the NK-T component's median log-gain at l* is within 0.1 of the random directions' (bootstrap), no layer localises the NK-T loss

E6.name: External confirmation (D11)
E6.dataset_criteria: CITE-seq with RNA counts, a published cell-type annotation, ADT that includes the gate proteins, never used in any teddy_mm analysis
E6.candidate: Hao et al. 2021 PBMC CITE-seq, GEO GSE164378 (3' data), present under data/raw/external_hao2021_gse164378 since 2026-09-30; not opened for this registration (no ADT names, values, RNA or labels read)
E6.frozen: TEDDY and the phase-1 head (no retraining), the evidence normaliser, panels, bars, classifier, gate logic and the annotation-map principles of this registration
E6.gate_thresholds: ADT CLR scales differ between datasets, so the BMMC thresholds do not transfer: the E6 primary key uses the registered per-batch estimator (gmm_nonzero_post50 within each external donor, label-free); annotation-only key reported too
E6.missing_proteins: a gate protein absent from the external panel drops the clause that uses it (CD335 -> NK count over the available NK markers, nk_min 2 kept; CD71 -> erythroid clause dropped); a panel protein absent -> that class is scored on its remaining panel proteins; listed in the addendum
E6.annotation_map: written from the external label names only and committed as an addendum (with sha256) before any external ADT or RNA value is read
E6.contamination: state whether GSE164378 is in TEDDY's pretraining corpus; if yes, label E6 'RNA possibly seen by TEDDY in pretraining'
E6.endpoints: E1's primary endpoints (E1.1a, E1.4a, E1.C2) and Q1 selective accuracy at matched coverage, per external donor
E6.replication: a v3 conclusion replicates if its sign holds in a majority of external donors and its two-stage bootstrap interval excludes 0 in the same direction
E6.failure: if annotation vs per-batch gate kappa < 0.70 on the external data, results are reported on the annotation-only key and labelled 'key not validated'
